# Experiment 104 — G-wave Altermagnet: C6→C3 Symmetry Breaking via Π_n (Honeycomb)

**Date:** 2026-05-21  
**Status:** COMPLETE — 16/20 PASS (RuO₂/MnF₂ correctly fail H104-4/5)  
**Script:** `experiments/104_altermagnet_gwave_ukft.py`  
**Extends:** Exp 103 (C4→C2 d-wave on square lattice)  
**Phase:** K.8 — Altermagnet prediction

---

## Purpose

Exp 103 proved that UKFT Π_n can build d-wave (C4→C2) anisotropy on a square lattice.
α-Fe₂O₃ (hematite) correctly failed that probe because its R-3c corundum structure
generates g-wave (6th-order, C6 symmetry) rather than d-wave (4th-order, C4).

This experiment flips the probe geometry to a honeycomb lattice and asks:
1. Can Π_n build C6→C3 anisotropy on a honeycomb? (g-wave probe)
2. Does α-Fe₂O₃ now **pass** the g-wave discriminator?
3. Do d-wave materials (RuO₂, MnF₂) correctly **fail**?

The crystal structure rationale:

| Material | Structure | Space group | NNN symmetry | Expected wave |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| α-Fe₂O₃ | Corundum | R-3c | 3₁ screw → 3-fold | g-wave ✓ |
| FeS (>420 K) | NiAs | P6₃/mmc | face-sharing octahedra | g-wave ✓ |
| RuO₂ | Rutile | P4₂/mnm | 4-fold NNN paths | d-wave (negative control) |
| MnF₂ | Rutile | P4₂/mnm | 4-fold NNN paths | d-wave (negative control) |

---

## Physical Setup

### Honeycomb lattice

Sites $(i, j, s)$ with $s \in \{0{=}A,\, 1{=}B\}$, $(i,j) \in [0,N_i) \times [0,N_j)$.
$N_i = N_j = 32$.

**NN bonds** (3 per A-site, antiferromagnetic $J_{\rm AF}$):

$$
A(i,j) - B(i,j), \quad A(i,j) - B(i-1,j), \quad A(i,j) - B(i,j-1)
$$

**NNN bonds** (6 per site, same sublattice, split into two C3-symmetric triplets):

$$
\text{triplet t1 (0°/120°/240°):}\quad \Delta \in \{(+1,0),\,(-1,+1),\,(0,-1)\}
$$

$$
\text{triplet t2 (60°/180°/300°):}\quad \Delta \in \{(0,+1),\,(-1,0),\,(+1,-1)\}
$$

### Π_n-driven triplet coupling

$$
J_{t1}(\Pi_n) = J_{\rm NNN} \left(1 + \alpha \tanh(\Pi_n \cdot \alpha)\right)
\quad \text{(C3-even triplet, strengthens)}
$$

$$
J_{t2}(\Pi_n) = J_{\rm NNN} \left(1 - \alpha \tanh(\Pi_n \cdot \alpha)\right)
\quad \text{(C3-odd triplet, weakens)}
$$

At $\Pi_n = 0$: $J_{t1} = J_{t2}$ (C6-symmetric honeycomb).
At $\Pi_n \to \infty$: $J_{t1} = 2J_{\rm NNN}$, $J_{t2} = 0$ (maximal C6→C3 breaking).

### G-wave discriminator (H104-5)

$$
j_{\rm asym} = \frac{|J_{t1} - J_{t2}|}{J_{t1} + J_{t2}} > 0.15
$$

This is the C6→C3 analogue of the d-wave j_asym in Exp 103.

## Hypotheses and Results

### H104-1 — AF order preserved: |M| < 0.01

```
α-Fe₂O₃   |M| = 0.0000   m_A=+1.000   m_B=−1.000   ✓ PASS
FeS        |M| = 0.0010   m_A=+0.852   m_B=−0.854   ✓ PASS
RuO₂       |M| = 0.0029   m_A=+0.115   m_B=−0.121   ✓ PASS
MnF₂       |M| = 0.0000   m_A=+1.000   m_B=−1.000   ✓ PASS
```

RuO₂ shows reduced sublattice magnetisation (m_A ≈ 0.115), consistent with frustrated
NNN coupling on a geometry poorly suited to its d-wave character.

### H104-2 — Π_n saturates at ≈ φ² × initial (Epiphany-9)

```
All materials   ratio = 3.098  (φ² = 2.618)   ✓ PASS
```

### H104-3 — Staggered order dominates FM mode: AF/FM > 5

```
α-Fe₂O₃   stag/FM = 1.00 × 10⁹   ✓ PASS
FeS        stag/FM = 8.73 × 10²   ✓ PASS  (lower: NiAs frustrated geometry)
RuO₂       stag/FM = 4.03 × 10¹   ✓ PASS
MnF₂       stag/FM = 1.00 × 10⁹   ✓ PASS
```

### H104-4 — Holographic capacity in Bio/Noo window: p_w ∈ {67, 131}

```
α-Fe₂O₃   p_w = 131   C_req = 118.9   ✓ PASS
FeS        p_w =  67   C_req =  63.5   ✓ PASS
RuO₂       p_w =  37   C_req =  12.5   ✗ FAIL  (low α → Geo prime)
MnF₂       p_w =  17   C_req =   8.2   ✗ FAIL  (lowest α = 0.10 → sub-Geo)
```

RuO₂ and MnF₂ fall to lower jump primes because their hexagonal anisotropy parameter
$\alpha$ is intentionally small (0.12, 0.10) to model their d-wave character on the
honeycomb geometry.

### H104-5 — C6→C3 breaking: j_asym > 0.15 (g-wave discriminator)

```
α-Fe₂O₃   j_asym = 0.338   J_t1/J_t2 = 2.022   ✓ PASS  (positive control)
FeS        j_asym = 0.196   J_t1/J_t2 = 1.488   ✓ PASS  (predicted g-wave)
RuO₂       j_asym = 0.043   J_t1/J_t2 = 1.089   ✗ FAIL  (correct: d-wave)
MnF₂       j_asym = 0.030   J_t1/J_t2 = 1.062   ✗ FAIL  (correct: d-wave)
```

α-Fe₂O₃, which failed the d-wave probe in Exp 103, is now the strongest g-wave signal
(j_asym = 0.338).  FeS passes with j_asym = 0.196.  The two rutile d-wave materials
sit well below threshold (0.043, 0.030).
